title: Thread-safe circuit breaker
idea: A thread-safe `ApiClient` shares one circuit breaker per downstream host, and every breaker change is a single compare-and-set, so no two threads can win the same transition.

analogy.text: A single key to a test room. Whoever takes the key from the hook runs the test; everyone else sees an empty hook.
analogy.breaks: A CAS loser is refused at once; nobody waits for the key back.

points: Many request threads share one client, so its breakers are shared state.
Check-then-act on the mode lets two threads both start a trial call.
Keep mode, failure count and open time in one immutable snapshot.
`computeIfAbsent` builds exactly one breaker per host under contention.

steps.caption: The cool-down has passed. Threads A and B call `allowRequest` at the same moment.
Unsafe version: A reads OPEN. Before A writes, B also reads OPEN.
Both write HALF_OPEN and both send a trial. A sick service gets two calls, not one.
Safe version: start again from OPEN with the same timing.
A runs `compareAndSet(OPEN, HALF_OPEN)`. The mode was still OPEN, so A wins.
B runs the same CAS. The mode is no longer OPEN, so it fails and B is rejected.
A's trial succeeds and the breaker closes. Exactly one probe reached the service.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier holds both threads at the worst moment, so the race shows on every run. Then the CAS fix.

walk.text: Two callers share one breaker and count how many trial calls they send.
Start both, join both, and only then print.
The barrier makes each thread wait until the other reaches the same point.
Read the mode, wait for the other thread, then act on that old read.
The CAS checks and writes in one step, so only one thread can win.

code.title: One breaker per host
code.caption: Eight threads call a broken host and a healthy one. Each host gets one breaker, and each ends in the right mode.

walk.text: Breakers by host in a ConcurrentHashMap; LongAdder counts calls with little contention.
Eight threads each send 500 calls to payments and 500 to search.
`computeIfAbsent` runs the factory at most once per host.
All breaker state is one immutable Snap held in an AtomicReference.
Only one thread can swap OPEN for HALF_OPEN, so only one trial runs.
Count and trip in one atomic update. The function may rerun, so it stays pure.

pitfalls: Do not keep mode and failure count in separate atomics; updates between them interleave.
Keep `updateAndGet` functions pure; under contention they may run more than once.
Always report the trial's outcome, even on exceptions, or HALF_OPEN never ends.

quiz.q: What does the first line of TrialRace print?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both threads read OPEN before either writes. Both then act on that read and send a trial.

takeaway: Hold breaker state in one snapshot and change it only by compare-and-set.

starters: Why not just make every breaker method synchronized?
Should the shared java.util.Random for jitter be per thread?
What happens if the trial call hangs forever?
